sources.title: Top Data Centres in Australia: 2026 Directory and Market Overview
sources.notes: 60 Hosting Certification Framework 'Certified Strategic' facilities across 13 providers; operator-by-operator site lists; NEXTDC M4 Fishermans Bend 162 MW / A$2bn approval January 2026; CDC Marsden Park 504 MW; Mandala 1,350 MW (2024) to 3,100 MW (2030); CBRE ~1.4 GW (2025) to ~1.8 GW (2028). REGRADED B to C on 2026-10-14: an aggregator's directory article that relays other firms' research (the Mandala and CBRE figures above are second-hand), which is class C under the rubric, as for the GovMarket aggregator. Not archived when read, so what it said on 18 September 2026 cannot be shown. Rows resting on it are to be re-sourced from primary records (RG-097).

set.summary: Certified Strategic is the highest designation and is required for sensitive and PROTECTED government workloads. CertifiedStrategic.com stated in March 2026 that 60 Certified Strategic facilities and enclaves are operated by 13 providers. Which agency administers the framework today is not established from a primary source here: releases up to v2.2.0 named the Digital Transformation Agency on the same article's authority, and that attribution is withdrawn pending the official register (RG-097).

set.notes: Named by CertifiedStrategic.com (March 2026) as administrator of the Hosting Certification Framework (Certified Strategic / Certified Assured). That attribution is withdrawn: it rests on a grade C aggregator and no primary source for it has been read. Which agency administers the framework today is open (RG-097).

60 Certified Strategic facilities and enclaves nationally across 13 providers, as CertifiedStrategic.com stated it in March 2026, unchanged during the certification pause. Not checked against the official register (RG-097). CORRECTED 2026-10-14: releases up to v2.2.0 tagged this national count with scope NSW.

Victorian Government development approval January 2026. Designed for AI, defence and sovereign technology workloads; rack densities above 1,000 kW; direct-to-chip liquid cooling. Capacity, cost and approval date rest on one grade C aggregator article, to be confirmed against NEXTDC's own announcement (RG-097).

research_gaps.question: Replace CertifiedStrategic.com (SRC_CERTSTRAT) with primary records for every row that rests on it: the official Hosting Certification Framework register for the Certified Strategic flags and the operational sites listed from it, NEXTDC's announcement for M4, and the original Mandala and CBRE reports for the four national capacity figures.
research_gaps.why_it_matters: One grade C aggregator article, never archived, is the sole source for 27 of the 93 sites and for 25 of the 26 Certified Strategic flags, and also supports 8 entities, the HCF instrument row, a security record, 5 metrics and 2 planning applications. The certified operational sites are the sovereign-hosting layer of the record, and today none of them has a primary source, a coordinate or a capacity.
research_gaps.target_source: https://www.hostingcertification.gov.au/certified-service-providers (archive with SHA-256); NEXTDC ASX announcement on M4 Fishermans Bend (January 2026); Mandala Partners, Data Centres as Enabling Infrastructure; CBRE Australian data centre report, August 2025
research_gaps.notes: LEADS ONLY, from search-engine summaries read on 2026-10-14 (below grade D, not relied on, and kept out of every fact row): the framework appears to have moved from the Digital Transformation Agency to the Department of Home Affairs on 1 May 2023, with registration of new providers and supplementary assessments paused from 3 November 2025; the register appears to list providers this database has no flag for (Australian Data Centres at Mitchell and Fyshwick, Cloud Carrier DB1, DigiCo BNE2 and SYD1, Fujitsu at Western Sydney and Homebush); the publisher's own pages appear to give 60, 61 and 62 certified sites; and press summaries give NEXTDC M4 as 150 MW as well as 162 MW. Also check whether the article supports ENT_VANTAGE and ENT_AUSTRALIANSUPER at all: both cite it for European and superannuation holdings that a directory article is unlikely to carry. The review found the article right where it copied a document directly: its 504 MW for Marsden Park matches the portal's power consumption, which this database had misfiled until RG-096.
